purpose: Test whether a receiver can recover 6-bit source identity through an underwater-acoustic-inspired multipath channel, and distinguish recoverable noise/channel effects from identity deliberately destroyed by a BA16-style quotient.

source_provenance.important_boundary: The executed run uses parameters/structure reproduced from the upstream open-source synthetic test fixture. It did NOT ingest the raw field-derived MAT files. Therefore it is an open-reference simulation, not measured-channel validation.

frozen_model.quotient_encoding: middle two bits j replaced by 00 before channel

42_collision.interpretation: 42 cannot be distinguished from 34, 38 or 46 once the middle two provenance bits are erased.

E1_full_vs_quotient_class.interpretation: As noise falls, the receiver approaches perfect recovery of what was actually encoded. Quotient-class recovery can become excellent, while exact j remains information-theoretically unavailable.

E3_j_leakage_classifier.method: StandardScaler + LogisticRegression on real+imag received samples; stratified 70/30 split
E3_j_leakage_classifier.multiple_testing_note: The nominal p=0.0316 at -5 dB is not evidence of leakage: three-SNR Bonferroni correction gives 0.0948, pooled test is non-significant, and the quotient construction makes the observation distribution independent of j.
E3_j_leakage_classifier.interpretation: No stable evidence that erased j survives the quotient; full encoding becomes highly learnable as SNR improves.

E4_channel_model_mismatch.interpretation: Even an injective source code is hard to invert with the wrong channel model. Reader = sensor alone is insufficient; calibration/channel-state provenance matters.

E5_receiver_array_diversity.key_result: At -20 dB, full-source recovery rose from 25.9% with one receiver to 61.2% with three; quotient-class recovery rose from 37.8% to 70.2%. Diversity improves preserved information but cannot recreate erased j.

E6_42_non_privilege_audit.interpretation: 42 was not granted any special decoder rule and lies within the ordinary codebook performance distribution. Model-specific differences between packet values reflect waveform/channel geometry, not semantic status.

captain_obvious_findings: Detecting a signal is easier than identifying its source.
A perfect receiver cannot infer bits deliberately removed before transmission without side information.
More sensors improve observability of preserved structure but do not reverse a many-to-one quotient.
An incorrect channel model can dominate decoding error even when SNR is high.
A one-off low p-value across several exploratory conditions must be corrected and checked against the construction.
Packet 42 must remain one member of a frozen codebook; no tuning is permitted around it.

raw_measured_data_gate.reason: The present execution environment could inspect the open-source toolchain and fixture but did not successfully ingest the large raw MAT channel/noise files.
raw_measured_data_gate.do_not_claim: No field-measured replay result is claimed in this receipt.
frozen_next_endpoints: mutual information / conditional entropy where estimable

seal: OBSERVABILITY CAN IMPROVE WITH MORE EARS; IDENTIFIABILITY CANNOT EXCEED THE PROVENANCE THAT SURVIVED THE CHANNEL.
